required_point_details.point: Section 35 provides the right to defend property against theft, which includes causing harm to the offender.
The harm caused must not exceed what is necessary and must remain within the restrictions of Section 37.
The right of private defence of property does not ordinarily extend to causing death unless the act falls under the categories in Section 41 (robbery, house-breaking after sunset, etc.).

final_answer_preview: Private defence can apply in situations where a person is attempting to prevent theft, as outlined in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. According to Section 35, individuals have the right to defend their own body and the body of others against offences affecting the human body, as well as to protect property against theft. Furthermore, Section 41 specifies that the right of private defence extends to causing harm to the wrong-doer if the act of theft creates a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt. Therefore, if your actions were in response to a theft and you had a reasonable belief that you needed to act to prevent harm, private defence may be applicable.
